title: Content revision: a missing tracked .gitattributes refuses the whole tree even when its directory is gone
outcome:
Follow-up from the tm-5gi4 phase 1 review pair on input c6140c01 (Claude Low, 2026-09-27; landed as acd7740).

src/content_revision.rs:144-154 fails the capture when a tracked .gitattributes is absent from the worktree, because Git would then take its attributes from the index. But content_revision_path (line 257) also returns None when a directory above the path is gone, and the refusal fires then too. So deleting a directory that holds a tracked nested .gitattributes (rm -rf subproject/) leaves the whole tree without a basis until the deletion is staged. A sparse checkout that excludes such a directory has no basis at all. That is a regression: schema-1 used git diff, which skips skip-worktree entries. With the directory gone, no file is left for those attributes to govern.

Fix: refuse only when the .gitattributes' parent directory exists (the path resolved but the file is absent). Test: a deleted directory holding a tracked .gitattributes keeps a revision; a sparse checkout excluding one keeps a revision.

Related edge found while checking this (Opus): a tracked .gitattributes replaced by a directory takes the is_dir branch (line 157) and is skipped rather than refused. Git reading attributes on Windows would then fall back to the index, just as for a missing file. Decide together whether that case refuses too.
